subject: DPA review, subprocessor mapping and breach-notice SLAs
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brighthealth.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@brighthealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA review and subprocessor mapping request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are BrightHealth's redlines to Redwood's standard DPA. Two items we need to address before we can move to signature:

- Subprocessor disclosure: please provide a current mapping of subprocessors and where that mapping will be hosted (we prefer a stable URL rather than attachments in email).
- Breach notification/forensic timelines: our security team asks for an explicit timeline for initial notification, forensic updates, and final root-cause deliverable. Our current ask is initial notification within 72 hours of confirmation, an initial investigational report within 7 days, and a final root-cause within 30 days.

Also can you confirm whether Redwood plans to use DocuSign or Adobe Sign for execution? We prefer DocuSign and like to capture the envelope link in our procurement system.

Attached: BrightHealth_DPA_redlines_2026-05-12.pdf

Looking forward to your response.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Senior Counsel, BrightHealth AI

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@brighthealth.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessor mapping request

Jordan —

Thanks, this is clear and helpful. Quick responses inline below and a proposed path to get to signature:

- Subprocessor mapping: attached is our current mapping (Redwood_subprocessors_2026-05-12.csv). We maintain a canonical list at https://subprocessors.redwood.ai/bh (will provide access link with auth token when we prepare the contract package).

- Breach notification / timelines: our security and legal teams propose the following compromise to balance timely notification and investigative accuracy:
  * Initial notification: within 48 hours of confirming unauthorized access to Personal Data (we will notify earlier if we have confirmed exposure).
  * Preliminary investigational findings: within 7 days with updates every 48 hours while active investigation continues.
  * Final root-cause and remediation summary: targeted within 45 days for complex incidents; we will provide a plan and ETA in the 7-day prelim report.

We appreciate BrightHealth's request for a 30-day final report; operationally some incidents require longer to fully remediate (e.g., cross-regional forensic collection). The 45-day target provides room for complex cases while committing to an early 7-day checkpoint.

- Subprocessor notice: we can commit to posting the canonical list at the URL above and will provide at least 30 days' notice prior to onboarding any new subprocessor; for security/hosting-critical subprocessors we will provide an emergency notice window and a right-to-object process (details we can add to the DPA).

- Execution: we will use DocuSign and will circulate the envelope for countersignature. Target to have DocuSign envelope to you by Fri 2026-05-21.

I've looped in Mina (Legal) and Ben (SE) to confirm the operational commitments and any redline language suggestions. If this looks acceptable I will prepare a countersigned DPA via DocuSign and attach the envelope link.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0134

Attachment: Redwood_subprocessors_2026-05-12.csv

From: Legal Ops <legalops@brighthealth.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brighthealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessor mapping request

Rachel —

Thanks for the quick reply and the mapping. A few points from our side after an initial review of your proposed compromise:

1) Notification timing: BH prefers the 72-hour initial notification standard (start of clock when Redwood reasonably suspects unauthorized access that affects Personal Data), rather than 48 hours.

2) Forensic deliverables: we need an explicit commitment for an "initial investigational report" within 7 days. Subsequent cadence can be flexible, but the 7-day milestone is important for our incident response process.

3) Subprocessor prior notice: 30 days is acceptable. However, for subprocessors that will process health data we require the ability to object and, if necessary, an alternative routing plan (similar to a right-to-object clause).

4) DocuSign: please include the envelope ID and a downloadable PDF of the executed DPA for our procurement system.

If you can confirm the 72-hour initial notice and the 7-day initial investigational report, we'll proceed with countersignature.

Regards,
BrightHealth Legal Ops

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Legal Ops <legalops@brighthealth.ai>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessor mapping request

Team —

Looping in Mina (legal) and Marcus (Security) to confirm operational acceptance and to propose final language we can include in the DPA. Short version: we can accept 72 hours for "initial notification" and commit to the 7-day "initial investigational report" milestone. Operational clarifications below: 

- 72-hour initial notice: Redwood will notify BrightHealth within 72 hours of confirming unauthorized access affecting Personal Data. If we have confirmed exposure earlier, we will notify immediately and mark the ticket as a high-priority incident.

- 7-day investigational report: Marcus, can your team commit to producing a preliminary investigational report within 7 days and provide daily or every-other-day updates while the investigation is active?

- Final report / remediation window: Redwood will provide a remediation plan and ETA in the 7-day report and aim for a final root-cause and remediation summary within 45 days for complex incidents.

- Subprocessor objection: we agree to 30 days' notice and will include an objection right scoped to subprocessors that will materially process health data; we'll add a short decision process (BrightHealth raises objection in writing within 15 days; parties use good faith to remediate, with escalations to legal owners).

If that aligns with BrightHealth's needs we will update the DPA with this language and route the DocuSign envelope. Would you please confirm target countersign date of Fri 21 May?

Thanks —
Rachel

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessor mapping request (operational confirmation)

Mina / Rachel —

Operational note from security: we can commit to the following for the DPA language and the security addendum: 

- Initial notification: Redwood Security will notify BrightHealth within 72 hours of confirming unauthorized access that affects Personal Data.
- Initial investigational report: preliminary findings within 7 calendar days, including scope of affected systems, likely data categories, and next steps.
- Ongoing updates: at minimum every 48 hours while active.
- Final report: target within 45 days; for complex cross-border investigations we may require up to 90 days, but we will communicate any ETA changes at the 7-day checkpoint.

We will also provide SOC 2 report and any other attestation references via a secure link upon countersignature. For subprocessor mapping we will provide the canonical URL and an authenticated download for procurement.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA review and subprocessor mapping request — countersignature

Rachel / Mina —

Thanks — the language looks acceptable on our side. We confirm BrightHealth will accept:

- 72-hour initial notification (clock starts when Redwood reasonably suspects unauthorized access affecting Personal Data).
- 7-day initial investigational report with at least 48-hour update cadence while investigation is active.
- Final root-cause and remediation summary targeted at 45 days, with a note that certain complex investigations may extend; we expect the ETA update in the 7-day report.
- 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors; right to object for health-data-critical subprocessors with a 15-day objection window.

DocuSign: attached is the executed envelope PDF (DocuSign_Envelope_BH-4421.pdf). Please provide the canonical subprocessor URL and SOC2 link (they will be recorded in our procurement system).

We appreciate the collaborative approach. Looking forward to working together.

Best,
BrightHealth Legal Ops
